summary: Feed s163_triple to IDS is degraded: 6.6% TCP packet loss plus 73.5% encrypted bytes (above 60% tolerance) and 29.1% VXLAN-encapsulated traffic significantly reduce detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or SPAN/mirror source is dropping packets under load - 210 of 3180 TCP packets (6.6%, threshold 1%) show TCP sequence gaps/retransmission evidence. Tool overload check is healthy, so loss is upstream of the IDS tool port, likely SPAN oversubscription or packet broker buffer exhaustion/burst drops.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_full_payload and both directions to reassemble streams; missing segments break TCP reassembly, cause flow timeouts and missed signatures, allowing evasion and false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute load across multiple IDS instances or broker egress ports to eliminate buffer drops and ensure complete TCP stream delivery; if source is SPAN, also replace SPAN with TAP for lossless capture.

findings.root_cause: 74% of bytes are encrypted (threshold 60% for this IDS). Traffic is predominantly TLS/encrypted, so IDS sees only ciphertext and handshake metadata.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires full payload inspection; with 73.5% encrypted share it cannot match payload signatures, reducing detection coverage to metadata only and missing malware/C2/exploit payloads inside encryption.

recommended_fix.why: Provide decrypted copy via broker-integrated or out-of-band TLS decryption (with proper keys/policy) or feed relevant plaintext from proxy, so IDS can inspect payload while respecting privacy/compliance.

findings.root_cause: 942 of 3238 frames (29.1%, threshold 10%) arrive inside VXLAN tunnel. Packet broker is forwarding encapsulated traffic without stripping outer header.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS sees outer VXLAN/IP/UDP header only and cannot parse inner Ethernet/IP payload; signatures and protocol decoders fail on encapsulated traffic, missing lateral movement and inner exploits.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to terminate/strip VXLAN headers and forward inner frames to IDS, preserving inner 5-tuple so IDS can correctly decode and detect.
